title: AIMO Interpretability Challenge
abstract: arXiv:2607.13899v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We propose the AIMO Interpretability Challenge, a competition on distinguishing robust from spurious reasoning in frontier mathematical language models based on the models' internal mechanisms. The challenge is motivated by a central limitation of standard reasoning benchmarks: strong final-answer accuracy does not reveal whether a model relies on stable reasoning mechanisms or exploits brittle reasoning shortcuts. Building on AI Mathematical Olympiad (AIMO) problems and submissions, together with resources from the Fields Model Initiative, the competition will provide (1) newly-published olympiad-level math reasoning problems and their symbolic representations, allowing generation of novel functional variants, (2) access to frontier reasoning models, and (3) assessments of models' adversarial robustness on these problems. translated_abstract: 我们提出了AIMO可解释性挑战赛，这是一项基于模型内部机制来区分前沿数学语言模型中稳健推理与虚假推理的竞赛。该挑战赛的动机源于标准推理基准测试的一个核心局限性：较高的最终答案准确率并不能揭示模型究竟是依赖稳定的推理机制，还是利用了脆弱的推理捷径。基于AI数学奥林匹克竞赛（AIMO）的题目与提交方案，并结合菲尔兹模型计划（Fields Model Initiative）的资源，该竞赛将提供：（1）新发布的奥林匹克级别数学推理题目及其符号表示，可用于生成新颖的功能变体；（2）前沿推理模型的访问权限；（3）模型在这些问题上对抗性鲁棒性的评估。参赛者将利用这些资源以及我们提供的计算基础设施支持，开发用于（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出了AIMO可解释性挑战赛，通过提供奥林匹克级数学题目、前沿推理模型访问权限和对抗性鲁棒性评估等资源，旨在基于模型内部机制区分前沿数学语言模型的稳健推理与虚假推理，弥补标准基准测试无法揭示模型是否依赖脆弱推理捷径的核心局限。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes the AIMO Interpretability Challenge, a competition providing olympiad-level math problems, access to frontier reasoning models, and adversarial robustness assessments to distinguish robust from spurious reasoning in mathematical language models based on their internal mechanisms, addressing the core limitation that strong final-answer accuracy does not reveal reliance on brittle reasoning shortcuts.
